summary: Final independent verification of revision 5 of the knee-edge OOD draft before A1: three lenses, skeptic re-check, readiness critic

packed.verdict: Revision 5 resolves 9 of the 10 r4 items in substance. The exception is item 9: its citation alignment was not done. The core changes hold up when re-derived. The identity H = G + (D_nsC - D_sC) is algebraically exact, and corr(G,H) = 0.50 in my 400k-draw rerun. The R3 bar of -1.5 and its conditional figures (0.86/0.48/0.12) and unconditional figures (0.70/0.30) match `screens/stage2_oc.py`, and the script's sha256 hashes match Part 11. The 21-branch Stage 2 still supplies every gated or reported rule: R1-R3, recovery, repair screens, D2 (computed at the fork), damage reproduced, the 9 differences and the Part 7 scaling. The A5 precondition and V0-S2 (now including the distance branch) are correct. Revision 5 is still not ready to call "100% certain". It introduces one new numerical error: the "BCA beats distance by 3" column of the joint operating characteristics is computed with an independent R2 draw. That understates the null (4.1% quoted vs 5.6% recomputed), the power (14.7% vs 17.8%) and the cost case (8.2% vs 9.6%), and Part 8.7's "2-4%" null range follows from it. The remaining problems are low-severity precision issues in text that A1 code would implement literally: (1) K1a's worst-case condition is stated in the wrong direction; (2) V0's items (a)-(e) now sit inside the new "Anchor sets" bullet; (3) item 5 under RANDOM's continuation is not said to be a gate or a filter; (4) the onset contrast can still trigger an INCOMPLETE through the 30-minute step cap, and it names no critic; (5) R_lin's a1..a3 convention is unstated; (6) the 9-difference noise check is not like-for-like; (7) two rerun-rule edge cases remain. None of these changes gate logic. All are fixable in one text-and-script pass (pass the same noise draws to R2 in stage2_oc.py and rerun it). After that pass, A1 can be approved on solid footing.

low_findings.claim: The new K1a worst-case condition, 'reachable only when rho under CUTOFF's continuation is at least about rho_R', is a sufficient condition stated as a necessary one. Part 8.2's 'clearly smaller' inherits the error. The worst case also mixes anchor sets: K1a is a median over the common gated anchors, while V0(b) bounds KC_R only on the subset that is predictor-valid under RANDOM's continuation, and a median of differences is not a difference of medians.
low_findings.evidence: The worst case is rho_C - 0.4 rho_R >= 0.5, which holds exactly when rho_C >= 0.5 + 0.4 rho_R. With rho_R = 2.0 and rho_C = 1.5, the value is 1.5 - 0.8 = 0.7 >= 0.5, so K1a is reachable even though rho_C < rho_R. The condition rho_C >= rho_R (both >= 0.85) only guarantees reachability, via 0.6 rho_C >= 0.51. V0(b) at :588 is stated 'at the same anchors', meaning the predictor-valid subset, while K1a at :598 uses the common anchors.
low_findings.fix: State that the worst case reaches 0.5 exactly when median rho_hat_C(s05) >= 0.5 + 0.4 x median rho_hat_R(s05). Say rho_C >= rho_R is sufficient, not necessary, and use the same condition in Part 8.2. Note that V0(b)'s KC_R bound is evaluated on a subset of K1a's anchors, so the worst case is approximate.

low_findings.claim: Inserting the 'Anchor sets' bullet re-parents V0's items (a)-(e): in the Markdown they are now sub-bullets of 'Anchor sets', not of V0. The preamble also still says 'anchors common to all arms', while the new definition says 'valid in every arm compared'. Item 5 under RANDOM's continuation is not called a gate (the >= 90% aggregate rule, INCONCLUSIVE on a miss, as V0(d) uses for CUTOFF) or only a per-anchor filter (floored at 32 of 48, about 67%).
low_findings.evidence: :582 is '- **Anchor sets.**', and :583-584 and :585-593 ((a)-(e)) share the same two-space indent. In r4, (a)-(e) followed the V0 bullet directly. Line 578 says 'common to all arms', and :565 says 'common to all arms within a world'. :583 says only 'with item 5 evaluated there'. L2 defines item 5 as an aggregate at >= 90% of anchors (:184), while 'predictor-valid anchor' (:54) is a per-anchor test.
low_findings.fix: Move 'Anchor sets' above or below the V0 block, or indent (a)-(e) under V0 again. Make the preamble say 'common gated anchors (defined below)'. State explicitly whether item 5 under RANDOM's continuation must pass at >= 90% (INCONCLUSIVE otherwise) or only filters anchors for V0(b) under V0(c)'s floor of 32.

If that time cap binds while the onset contrast, which runs last, is executing, the result is an exhausted cap, which 5.0 labels INCOMPLETE. The Q^pi rollouts that select F's population, R_lin's Q^pi(-0.5) and Q^pi(-0.25) for steep probes, are not given an a1..a3 convention or a source (saved JSON or new replay).

low_findings.claim: The 9 replicate-minus-Stage-1-native differences do not test the SD 3.55 assumption like-for-like. The 3.55 comes from same-fork BCA-minus-native pairs that share common random numbers: the prior branch() folds the same branch_native_seed into the fork rng with no arm term. The replicate and the Stage 1 native branch deliberately use different seeds and minibatch streams.
low_findings.evidence: runtime.py :226-228 uses the same seed for every arm, so prior BCA and native branches shared random numbers. Stage 2 asserts that the replicate's minibatch digest differs from the Stage 1 branch's (:643). The model in stage2_oc.py fixes the same-fork difference SD at 3.55. A non-CRN native-native difference measures sqrt(2) x the unshared branch noise, plus Stage 1's selection for damage.
low_findings.fix: Describe the 9 differences as an upper-side noise check without common random numbers, which is expected to exceed the CRN figure of 3.55, or report them without calling them a check of 3.55.

low_findings.claim: The revised rule still leaves two edge cases. 'Same check' allows a unit that fails a different tolerance check on each rerun under unchanged code to be rerun again, which re-rolls GPU nondeterminism once per check. And 'under unchanged code' does not say what it is compared with, after the one permitted code-only fix.
low_findings.evidence: :435 reads 'A second failure of the same unit on the same check, under unchanged code, makes the step INCONCLUSIVE'. One possible sequence: fail on check A, rerun, fail on check B, rerun, pass. That uses two re-rolls without triggering the rule.
low_findings.fix: Trigger INCONCLUSIVE on any second failure of the same unit under unchanged code (any check). Define 'unchanged' relative to the code of that unit's previous attempt.

packed.verdict: Revision 5 gets the OOD definition itself right. I checked it against the simulator and host code. L1 (strict |a0| > KNEE on the executed float32 command, CUTOFF with zero W rows, censored rather than unsupported recorder support) holds. So do the L2.1 identity and the L2.2 bit-identity of thrust on the supported region (canonical thrusterchain.py 155-160, 163-182). The host objective the protocol relies on also matches td3_bc.py 228-238 and candidate.py 76-86: per-dimension mean BC, so pi0 = m + 2 lambda dQ1/da0; Q1 in the actor; stop-gradient lambda; twin-minimum target with smoothing. The kill rules are built so that PASS requires real withholding, Q-driven entry and harm that comes from the knee: K1a against labelled RANDOM, K2 against the inward BC pull, K3a and K3c as within-policy contrasts plus the world swap. I found no path to a false PASS of the condition. The label precedence covers every step. I am not giving the 100% certainty the user asked for, for three reasons. (1) The L2 and V0 floors are absolute value-gap numbers. That gap is not a property of the region alone: it shrinks roughly in proportion to how well the continuation policy keeps states small. In dynamics-only proxies (I did not use the old actors), a competent clipped continuation gives median rho(s05) of about 0.6, below the sealed 0.85 floor, and only 57% of anchors reach 0.4 against the 70% required. So step 0.4 could FAIL, or Stage 1 could end permanently INCONCLUSIVE, because the learners are competent rather than because the OOD situation is absent. The s05 floor was derived from K1a's arithmetic, never screened. (2) Nothing certifies that collection, replay and evaluation actually run at stall_slope 3.0. The canonical code and the environment both default to 1.5. (3) The new critic forward-pass path behind KC, which is the core L3 measurement, has no known-answer check, even though saved per-probe Q1 values exist. All three are cheap to fix. A1 seals the thresholds, so they should be fixed or explicitly accepted before approving A1.

low_findings.claim: D1/D2 do not name their anchor set. Stage 1's anchors are 'never reused in Stage 2' (:557), and Stage 2's 64 fresh anchors are described as the 20k evaluation bank (:646). It is therefore undefined which states the 10k AUROC is computed at, so that set could be chosen after the fact. The a1..a3 convention (the actor's values) also differs from the gated KC convention (a1..a3 = 0) at the same slots without a stated reason.
low_findings.fix: Name a dedicated, seeded E2 anchor stream for the precheck in seeds.json, or state that it uses the Stage 2 anchors. Either justify the a1..a3 convention or align it with KC.

low_findings.claim: PROMISING can be issued in a seed where the native replicate shows no damage (K2/K3a not met). There G > 0 is noise and does not show BCA repairing OOD harm. Not gating on damage is a sound way to avoid selection bias, but the label then has no fixed reading for that case.
low_findings.evidence: 'Reported, not gated: damage reproduced' (:663). R1's null pass rate is about 8.5% (stage2_oc_output.txt).
low_findings.fix: Pre-register a qualifier: PROMISING is reported as 'PROMISING (damage not reproduced in seed i)' whenever the replicate misses K2 or K3a, and that seed's G is not read as repair.

verified.section: Part 2 L2 PASS rule items 1-4 (DRAFT_PROTOCOL.md:183-190); Stage 1 V0(b) floor and V0(d) (:586-592); step 0.1 value estimate (:461); step 0.4 FAIL row (:538)
verified.claim: The L2 model-relevance floors are absolute value-gap numbers (median rho_hat(s05) >= 0.85, >= 70% of anchors at >= 0.4, drop >= 0.25 at >= 70%). rho is the one-step gap under a stated continuation, and it scales with how large that continuation lets the state get. A competent continuation can therefore fail these floors even though the region is fully withheld and the stall is fully present. Step 0.4 would then record FAIL ('not shown model-relevant'), or Stage 1 V0(b)/V0(d) would end INCONCLUSIVE with no re-attempt allowed, for a reason unrelated to the OOD condition. The s05 floor was derived from K1a's arithmetic (0.6 x rho >= 0.5) and was never screened. Step 0.1 estimated rho only near s10, from old-critic quadratic fits.
verified.evidence:
Proxy computed with canonical dynamics() on synthetic arrays only (scratchpad verify_wf_r5/fresh/rho_proxy.py, rho_lqr.py, rho_pool.py). Setup: E2 starts, recorder-prefix anchors at t in {0, 25, 50} in the stall-3.0 world, forced a0 with a1..a3 = 0. Exact Q_nostall - Q_stall by continuation:
- Zero-action continuation: pooled median rho(s05) 2.29 (91% >= 0.4), rho(s10) 4.69.
- Clipped discounted-LQR continuation (median Q about -70): pooled median rho(s05) 0.61 (57% >= 0.4), rho(s10) 1.31 (63% >= 0.5), rho(s20) >= 1.0 at only 66%. Items 1-3 would fail.
- Open-loop a = -0.7 continuation at t=0 (median Q -161): rho(s05) 0.67 (55% >= 0.4); drop >= 0.25 at only 63%.
The old full-data native 20k actors return -137 to -155 at strong current (run/evaluation/seed*_full__native__20000__strong_current.json), about the competence of the -0.7 proxy. The new learners will train on deep-current data and should do better. Across all proxies the ratio rho(s05)/rho(s10) is about 0.46, so step 0.1's 2.12-2.58 near s10 implies about 1.0-1.2 at s05 only if the continuation is as weak as that estimate assumed.
verified.fix: Before sealing at A1, add a dynamics-only screen (pure canonical functions, no checkpoints). Compute rho(s05), rho(s10), rho(s20) and the drop at E2 gated anchors under a ladder of continuations, from zero action through clipped LQR. Then either set the floors from that screen or reference them to the continuation (for example, gate V0(b) and K1a as ratios to rho). Alternatively, move K1a and V0(b) to a depth where rho is larger while RANDOM still has labels. State in L2 that rho scales with the state magnitude under the continuation, so a step 0.4 PASS under the old actors does not carry over to Stage 1 learners. Disclose in Part 8 the risk that competent learners end Stage 1 INCONCLUSIVE.

check.reason: Partly refuted. The step 0.4 part does not hold. Under the actual step 0.4 continuation (the old full-data native 20k actors), the saved exact Q^pi already implies rho well above every L2 floor at strong current, so a step 0.4 FAIL for this reason is unlikely. The Stage 1 part stands. rho scales with how far the continuation lets the state drift. In saved Q^pi for the same actors, ordinary-context probes give rho(s05) of about 0.65-0.71, below 0.85; strong-current probes give 1.13-1.45. The clipped-LQR proxy gives 0.61. V0(b) puts the absolute 0.85 floor on rho under RANDOM's own continuation. The hypothesis itself predicts RANDOM is the more competent arm (J(RANDOM) > J(CUTOFF) is a pre-registered secondary), so this floor is the one most likely to miss. The miss would end Stage 1 INCONCLUSIVE even when K1a is fully testable. That is because the floor's stated purpose, worst-case K1a reachability (draft :197-200), depends on rho under CUTOFF, not on rho_R: a small rho_R makes the 0.4 x rho_R bound small, which helps K1a. Part 8.2 (:752-757) discloses INCONCLUSIVE only for fold carry-over and kink width, not for competence-driven small rho. Part 8.9 says only that the gap size is an estimate until step 0.4, which measures it under the old actors only. The result is a false-stop or wasted-compute risk, not a false-positive risk, so it is medium rather than high.
check.evidence: Draft :186 (item 1 median >= 0.85), :587 (V0(b) floor under RANDOM's own clipped continuation), :593 (V0(d) items 1-4 under CUTOFF's), :197-200 (floor justified by worst-case K1a), :752-757 (Part 8.2 omits this risk). The finder's pooled proxy was reproduced exactly: clipped LQR gives rho05 median 0.61 (57% >= 0.4), rho10 median 1.31 (63% >= 0.5), rho20 >= 1 at 66%; zero action gives 2.29 / 4.69. Independent check from saved JSON (skeptic_fresh/qpi_rho.py, run/evaluation/seed*_full__native__20000__*.json, high-load probes): take f(u) = qpi(u) + 0.3u^2, fit a quadratic on the forced slots {-0.5..0.5}, and set rho(s) = f(s) - f(T3(s)). At strong current, seeds 0/1/2 give rho05 medians 1.13 / 1.22 / 1.45 (84-88% >= 0.4), rho10 2.31 / 2.48 / 2.93, drop >= 0.25 at 91-97%, median Q -157 / -167 / -176, so step 0.4 would pass. In the ordinary context the same actors give rho05 0.65 / 0.69 / 0.71 (71% >= 0.4), rho20 >= 1 at only 76%, median Q -92 / -95 / -91, below the 0.85 floor. Across all continuations rho05 is roughly 0.0075 x |Q|, so V0(b)'s 0.85 floor needs RANDOM's E2 value at or below about -115.

verified.section: Part 4.6 host-config tests (:372); 4.7 replay and twin checks (:396-400); Part 3.4 worlds
verified.claim: No certification item asserts that collection, replay, anchor rebuilding, Q^pi evaluation and free rollouts run at stall_slope 3.0. The canonical Physics() default, the STALL constant and ThrusterChainEnv(stall_slope=1.5) all default to 1.5. Step 0.4 also evaluates a 1.5 world deliberately, so the evaluator handles both. If the whole study ran at slope 1.5 by mistake, every Part 4 check would still pass: the predicate does not depend on slope, and replay and twin checks would use the same wrong Physics. The L2.1 identity would catch it only if T is coded with a literal 3 rather than taken from physics.stall_slope. The study would then silently test about half the gap (Part 10: 0.60 against 1.18).
verified.evidence: canonical/thrusterchain.py: class Physics, stall_slope = 1.5 (around line 104), and STALL = Physics(). environment.py:56: __init__(..., stall_slope=1.5). datasets.py:170 stores Physics(stall, stall_slope). critic.certain_vs_measured:
CERTAIN (exact or provable from source and float32 arithmetic). KNEE = float32(0.8) = 0.800000011920929, and every Part 0 slot and depth, including float32(-0.9) lying outside R_deep-. T3(a0) = sign(a0)(KNEE - 3(|a0| - KNEE)), so T3(-0.9) = -0.5 and T3(-1) = -0.2. The L2.1 identity holds because the next state depends only on thrust and the reward charges 0.3 a^2 on the clipped command. Thrust is bit-identical between worlds for |a0| <= KNEE. Load g = c + w1 does not depend on actions, so recorder actions and masks are byte-identical across the twins. The host objective (td3_bc.py 186-245) uses per-dimension-mean BC, Q1 in the actor, a stop-gradient lambda = 2.5/mean|Q1| and a twin-minimum target with 0.2/0.5 smoothing, which gives pi0 = m + 2 lambda dQ1/da0. Under the TD3+BC per-tuple loss the region cannot be identified from retained support. Label precedence is exhaustive. No gate can PASS without the OOD condition: K1a compares against labelled RANDOM, every retained a0 >= -KNEE, and K3a/K3c are within-policy contrasts with the world swap. Exact algebra: H = G + (D_nsC - D_sC). The closed-form recorder figures are exact: CUTOFF anchor -0.7263, removed about 28.3k, P(g >= 0.4) = 0.575. Constants 0.22499999 and 0.168/0.288 are exact. Every Part 11 hash matches its file, and stage2_oc_output.txt reproduces byte-for-byte. Code citations are correct except the runtime.py seeding range.

MEASURED or MODEL-DEPENDENT (not certain). The rho magnitudes come from proxies: quadratic fits on old critics, saved Q^pi from old actors, and clipped-LQR and open-loop dynamics proxies. Whether Stage 1 learners clear the L2 and V0 floors is unknown until Stage 1 runs. The 0.4 coefficient's coverage of softplus widths 0.04-0.05 rests on a softplus kink model, not on measured RANDOM critics. Every Stage 2 operating characteristic (R1 about 8.5% null, P(R3|R1), joint pass rates) is Monte Carlo under an assumed Gaussian model with same-fork SD 3.55, itself estimated from 9 prior cells (SD 3.546), and an untested cross-world generic-gain assumption. The 'joint d=3' figures as published are also numerically wrong (about 5.6% null, not 4.1%). The 6-SD bounds and expected values for the recorder come from Monte Carlo. Timing and budget figures are extrapolated from saved receipts (about 500 s per branch, 5,031 transitions per second). The reach forecast and G0.5 margins come from old critics trained at slope 1.5. That a critic extrapolates smoothly, so that KC is about rho_hat, is an assumption the design tests rather than one it can guarantee.
residual_risks: Stopping without an answer: even after the fixes, Stage 1 can end INCONCLUSIVE for reasons unrelated to whether BCA helps. The RANDOM critic may not carry its low-load labels over to high load, it may round the stall kink more smoothly than the 0.4 allowance covers, or the learners may be competent enough that the value gap at s05 shrinks below a floor. These cost compute but cannot produce a false positive.

Value-gap size is an estimate: every number about how much the stall changes value at the gated depths comes from old critics, old actors or dynamics proxies. Step 0.4 measures it only for the old actors, and the new learners could behave differently.

Stage 2 is a weak screen: with 3 seeds and noise SD about 3.55, PROMISING has roughly a 2-6% false-pass rate and only about 5-18% power at a true +3 benefit. NOT-PROMISING says little against BCA. The noise figure is itself estimated from 9 earlier cells.
R3 assumes BCA's generic benefit is about the same in the stall and no-stall worlds. Nothing in the design tests this.

Implementation slips that certification will not catch until F2 and F3 are added: a run at the default stall_slope 1.5, or a forced-probe critic input built wrongly, would currently pass every listed check.
Smoothed target actions for CUTOFF fall in the withheld region about a third of the time. KC differencing assumes that contamination cancels, and the absolute error is only reported.

Checkpoint-to-checkpoint sign instability seen in the prior study (hole-vs-random gain flipping sign between 15k and 20k) means individual seeds can disagree. Gating on 20k only is correct, but results may look noisy.
Provenance relies on file mtimes and truncated hashes until the design folder is committed. Committing it needs the user's approval.
